FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 24 October 1988, after 
the draft finalized by the Pest Control Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural 
and Food Products Division Council. 

Ferbam WP are used as fungicides mainly for the protection of foliage. 

Ferbam WP are generally manufactured to contain 75 percent ( mim ) of ferbam. 

In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the 
Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restric- 
tions imposed under these, wherever applicable. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded 
off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. 'Rules for rounding off numereial values {revised)*. The 
number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the 
specified value in this standard.

powder, greyish-black in colour and shall wet

4 PACKING AND MARKING 

4.1 PacUiig 

The material shall be packed in mild steel or 
tinplate pr fibreboard containers lined with 
polyethylene of thickness not less than 0062 mm. 
In addition^ the material shall comply with the 

feneral packing requirements as given in 2 of 
S 8190 (Part 1 ) : 1980. 

4.2 Marking 

The containers shall be securely closed and shall 
bear legibly and indelibly the following informa- 
tion in addition to the information as required 
under the Insicticides Act, 1968 and Rules framed 
thereunder: 

a) Name of the material; 

b) Name of the manufacturer; 

c) Date of manufacture; 

d) Batch number; 

e) Net mass of contents; 

f ) Nominal ferbam content, percent by mass; 
and 

g) A cautionary notice worded as in the 
InstctUidiS Act, 1968 and Rules framed 
thereunder. 



4.2.1 The container may also be marked with 
the Standard Mark. 

5 SAMPLING 

Representative samples of the material shall be 
drawn in accordance with the procedure as 
prescribed in IS 10627 : 1983. 

6 TESTS 

6.1 Tests shall be carried out as prescribed in the 
appropriate annex and clauses given in Table 1. 
For estimating ferbam content, begin the test 
with sufficient quantity of sample containing 0*3 g 
of ferbam content. 

6.2 For carrying out suspensibility test, take an 
amount of the sample to form 2*5 percent ( m/o ) 
suspension. 

6.3 Qjnality of Reagents 

Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and 
distilled water {sa IS 1070 : 1977) shall be 
employed in tests. 

NOTE — 'Pure chemicalt* shall mean chemicals that do 
not contain impurities which affect the results of analysis. 



Stendard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act^ 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection* 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to 
that standard as a further safeguard* Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards.
